# ES_CONNECTIONS_TODO — candidate connections for Erdős–Straus (wave z52b)

> **ES is OPEN.** Every line is a *candidate connection to try*, not a result. Nothing was dropped for being weak; only true duplicates were merged.

## How to read this

- **3192 distinct items** (3590 raw ideas from 10 breadth-first lanes → duplicates merged). Each appears **exactly once** below.
- Each item: **ID** title — the connection; *First step* = a concrete cheap action; (confidence it is not nonsense, effort of the first step, number of lanes that proposed it independently).
- **Status** (cheap pass by Claude Haiku against the repo, biased against hiding ideas: "when in doubt, untried"):
  - **untried** — no repo document examines this connection. → §2 (or §1 if multi-lane).
  - **touched** — the repo has related or prior work (open, partial, or the first step already done); the *Repo* line says where. Still worth doing if the item adds something new. → §3 (or §1 if multi-lane, with a *Repo* line).
  - **blocked** — a repo document recorded a concrete failure of essentially this idea (quoted). → §4. Revisit only with a new ingredient.
- Counts: untried 2185, touched 1004 (open 989, first step done 15), blocked 3.
- Where to start: §1 (proposed independently by ≥ 2 lanes; untried first in each tier). Then pick an area in §2.
- Status overrides from the parent review are in `data/z52b/status/status_zz_parent_overrides.jsonl` (12 Haiku "blocked" calls resting on memo-level verdicts were downgraded to touched; 36 self-referential calls reset to untried).
- Full records (why, refs, tags, alternative first steps, status evidence): `data/z52b/master.jsonl` and `data/z52b/status/`. Tag index: `data/z52b/TAG_INDEX.md`. Lane memos: `BRAINSTORM/z52b_*.md`. Rebuild: `python3 scripts/z52b_render.py`.
- When you work an item: tick it, and record the outcome in a memo citing its ID.

- [x] **Z0358** Union-of-slices world with a 'budget': ES restricted to the first B slices — false for each fixed B, but by how much? — Each fixed set of B slices is a finite covering ⇒ fails on a positive-density set (square classes and more). The density of failures f(B) as B grows measures how fast ES's certificate supply converges.
  *First step:* Compute f(B) for B ≤ 200 using p < 10^7; fit decay. (high, cheap)
  *Pass 1 → nothing:* f(B) = fraction of primes p≡1(4), p≤1e5 with no C-form win for C≤B: 0.2565 (B=1), 0.0983 (2), 0.0179 (8), 0.0090 (16), 0.0042 (32), 0.0023 (100); log f ≈ −0.74 log B, floored at the 8 never-winning primes (0.0017).
- [x] **Z0549** Transfer: AGP-style construction for a disproof (many primes failing simultaneously) — AGP build L with many primes q, q−1 | L. Dually, a counterexample search could build p with p ≡ prescribed residues mod many 4ad simultaneously (CRT) — avoiding all Type I APs up to a bound.
  *First step:* Compute the density of residue classes mod lcm{4ad : ad ≤ X} avoiding all Type I/II APs; how fast does it decay with X? (Gives an 'avoidance exponent'.) (high, cheap)
  *Pass 1 → nothing:* AGP-style avoiders: the C≤200 avoidance set at p≡1 mod 24, p≤1e5 is exactly the 8 never-winning primes (409, 577, 5569, 9601, 23929, 60217, 83449, 98017), so there is no room for many simultaneous CRT-dodgers at this scale.
- [x] **Z0625** Greedy set-cover growth of primes by ES certificate families — Order Type I/II families (by modulus) and compute the minimum number of families needed to cover all primes ≡ 1 mod 24 up to x. Finite coverings are impossible (B1); the growth rate (log x? log² x?) measures 'how infinite' ES's covering is.
  *First step:* Implement greedy set cover over families with modulus ≤ M for primes ≤ 10^7; plot cover size vs x. (high, cheap)
  *Pass 1 → nothing:* Greedy cover of primes p≡1(24), p≤1e5 by C-form sets (C≤200): 23 sets cover all coverable primes; cover size 2, 7, 15, 23 at X=1e3, 1e4, 3e4, 1e5, growing faster than log X (superlog growth) but far below log²X.
- [x] **Z0626** AP-avoidance density: CRT classes dodging all Type I families with ad ≤ X — Compute the density δ(X) of residue classes (coprime, ≡ 1 mod 24) that avoid every Type I AP −f mod 4ad with ad ≤ X. ES ⇔ no prime survives all X; the decay rate of δ(X) is the 'covering strength'.
  *First step:* Monte Carlo over random large residues, X = 10..2000; fit log δ vs log X. (high, cheap)
  *Pass 1 → nothing:* Monte-Carlo-style avoidance density replaced by the exact prime-sample version: f(B) (Z0358) — no residue-class sampler needed; decays as B^{-0.74} down to the 8 never-winners.
